text: Lexmount Browser 是面向 DSH Web 和 Headless 环境的云端浏览器工具包，通过 Bundle 将原生工具接入 DSH，并由本地 Node 适配器调用独立 browser-cli。它可创建和管理浏览器会话与持久 Context，打开网页、等待页面元素或文本、点击和填写表单、读取页面快照，并生成截图或 PDF。用户可借助这些工具完成需要交互网页的自动化操作；首次调用会按平台准备 CLI，浏览器服务需要 Lexmount 账户认证。

Lexmount Browser adds cloud browser tools to DSH through a Bundle and Node adapter. It manages sessions and Contexts, opens pages, waits for text or selectors, clicks and fills controls, reads snapshots, and returns screenshots or PDFs. First use prepares browser-cli.
我想让 DSH 自动打开网页并查看页面内容。
有没有办法让 DSH 等网页上的某个按钮或文字出现？
我需要让 DSH 在浏览器里点按钮并填写表单。
想用 DSH 截取网页长图并保存成附件。
怎么让 DSH 保留浏览器登录状态，后续任务继续使用？
DSH 能不能把浏览网页生成的 PDF 保存到指定位置？
I want DSH to inspect and interact with pages in a cloud browser.
Can DSH wait for page text, click controls, and fill forms?
Lexmount Browser 的功能「会话与持久 Context」：创建、查询和关闭云端浏览器会话，也可创建或选择持久 Context 来复用浏览状态。通过对应 DSH 工具传入会话或 Context 参数。
Lexmount Browser 的功能「网页交互」：打开 URL、等待 CSS 选择器或页面文本，再点击匹配元素或填写表单控件；每项由独立浏览器工具调用并返回结果。
Lexmount Browser 的功能「页面检查与截图」：读取当前页面 URL、标题、文本和 HTML 快照，或截取 PNG 并作为 DSH 图片附件返回；可选将截图保存到指定路径。
Lexmount Browser 的功能「PDF 导出」：调用 browser-cli 将当前浏览器页面输出为 PDF 文件，可指定主机上的目标路径及是否包含 CSS 背景。

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · `@lexmount/dsh-browser`：Lexmount cloud browser tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). This package is a lightweight DSH Bundle: it registers native model tools and invokes the Rust `browser-cli`, but it does not contain a native executable, run an MCP server, or depend on the Lexmount Node.js SDK.

> Status: Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Linux x64 native validation is complete. The current stable Bundle version is `0.1.1`.
@lexmount/dsh-browser README · `@lexmount/dsh-browser`：> **Current platform support:** Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Linux x64. macOS Intel and Linux ARM64 are not currently supported.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Runtime architecture：```text
DSH Web / Headless
  → @lexmount/dsh-browser (Bundle and Node adapter only)
  → pinned browser-cli download and user cache
  → browser-cli child process

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Runtime architecture：The Bundle registers tools without accessing the network. On the first tool call it selects the current OS/CPU asset, downloads the pinned `browser-cli` release and `SHA256SUMS` from Lexmount's versioned Tencent COS path, verifies the digest, executable format/architecture, and CLI version, then installs it atomically in a user cache. Later calls and restarts reuse the verified cache, so an already populated cache works offline.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Runtime architecture：The npm tarball contains no `browser-cli` or `browser-cli.exe` file. End users do not need Rust, Python, a browser driver, or an npm lifecycle script.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Platform status：| Host | Release asset target | Current status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` | Supported |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `aarch64-apple-darwin` | Supported |
| Linux x64 | `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl` | Supported |
| macOS Intel | `x86_64-apple-darwin` | Not currently supported; asset missing |
| Linux ARM64 | — | Not currently supported; asset missing |

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Platform status：`native-source.json` pins `browser-cli` v1.1.15 at commit `952a5e53ff9dd3980342d4dae7f860f80b39a100`. The Windows asset statically links the C runtime, and the Linux x64 asset is a static musl executable. This Bundle uses the three assets published by that immutable release. Adding another platform requires a new browser-cli version and a new npm package version with fresh validation; it will not mutate this release in place.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Install：The current release requires Node.js `>=22.14.0`, DSH `0.1.0-rc.6`, and a
`pnpm` executable on `PATH`. The commands below use `npx`, so a global DSH
installation is not required. The commands pin the Bundle version so DSH's
dependency release-age policy cannot resolve the request to an older release.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Windows x64：Open a normal, non-administrator PowerShell in the directory that should become
the DSH workspace, then run:

```powershell
node --version
corepack --version
corepack install --global pnpm@11.22.0
corepack enable pnpm

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Windows x64：If `corepack enable pnpm` reports an access error under
`C:\Program Files\nodejs`, run only the Corepack setup commands once from an
administrator PowerShell, close it, and run DSH itself as the normal user. If
port `3080` is already occupied, start DSH on an OS-assigned free port and open
the URL it prints:

```powershell
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 web --port 0
```

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · macOS Apple Silicon：This release supports Apple Silicon only. Confirm that the machine reports
`arm64`; `x86_64` means an Intel Mac and is not currently supported. In
Terminal, change to the directory that should become the DSH workspace, then
run:

```bash
uname -m
node --version
corepack --version
corepack install --global pnpm@11.22.0

If port `3080` is already occupied, use an OS-assigned free port and open the
printed URL:

```bash
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 web --port 0
```

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Linux x64：Confirm that the machine reports `x86_64`, then run:

```bash
uname -m
node --version
corepack --version
corepack install --global pnpm@11.22.0

If port `3080` is already occupied, use an OS-assigned free port and open the
printed URL:

```bash
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 web --port 0
```

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Linux x64：DSH RC.6 delegates plugin installation to a `pnpm` executable on `PATH`; it does
not bundle that executable. If Corepack cannot create the shim, install pnpm
through the normal Node package-manager setup and verify `pnpm --version`
first.

If DSH was already running while the Bundle was installed or updated, stop and
restart it before testing. Package installation does not hot-load a new Bundle
into an existing Web process.

For unattended use, install the same Bundle into the Headless profile:

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Linux x64：```bash
npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 plugin --profile headless add @lexmount/dsh-browser@0.1.1
```

The supported Harness range is `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0`. DSH remains a release
candidate, so each DSH upgrade requires installation and tool-registration
regression testing.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · First use and cache：1. Run `lexmount_doctor`. The first call may download the current platform executable.
2. If credentials are missing, run `lexmount_auth_login` from the interactive Web profile and approve access in the system browser.
3. Create a temporary Session, or select/create a persistent Context when login state must be reused.
4. Navigate, inspect with `lexmount_browser_snapshot`, then use typed wait/click/fill tools.
5. Close temporary Sessions when finished.

Default cache locations are:

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · First use and cache：| Platform | Cache root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Lexmount\dsh-browser` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Caches/Lexmount/dsh-browser` |
| Linux | `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/lexmount/dsh-browser` or `~/.cache/lexmount/dsh-browser` |

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · First use and cache：Set `LEXMOUNT_BROWSER_CLI_CACHE_DIR` to choose another cache root. `LEXMOUNT_BROWSER_CLI_PATH` is an explicit administrator/developer override for a preinstalled CLI; that path is still checked for format and version, but its trust is controlled by whoever sets the environment variable.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · First use and cache：The login flow stores credentials at the existing `browser-cli` location and never asks the user to paste an API key into chat. Headless runs must authenticate beforehand because the PKCE flow requires an interactive system browser.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Tool surface：Screenshot results are persisted through the DSH image attachment service. PDF and download tools write to the requested host path and return that path because DSH `0.1.0-rc.6` has no generic binary attachment content block.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Security and behavior：- Downloads use a fixed HTTPS origin and version path. The matching `SHA256SUMS` entry, executable format, platform architecture, expected CLI version, and cache metadata are verified before execution.
- A cancelled first call cancels its download when no other call is waiting. Plugin disposal cancels downloads and terminates owned child processes.
- Model input is passed as a child-process argument array with `shell: false`; it is never concatenated into a shell command.
- API keys, Authorization fields, `ws`, and Chrome DevTools WebSocket URLs are removed from returned data and diagnostics.
- Tool guidance tells the model to obtain user confirmation before purchases, publication, destructive remote actions, and account/security changes.
- JavaScript evaluation and raw CDP remain model-visible for advanced browser automation.
@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Security and behavior：DSH RC.6 does not expose MCP-style side-effect annotations on native tools. UI presentation categories are not permission enforcement.

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm run check
npm run package:verify
```

On a currently supported host, test a locally built v1.1.15 CLI without changing the package:

```bash
LEXMOUNT_BROWSER_CLI_PATH=/absolute/path/to/browser-cli npm run test:native
```

Verify the pinned remote assets, then run the real current-platform integration test on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, or Linux x64:

```bash
npm run native:assets
npm run test:native
```

@lexmount/dsh-browser README · Development：The `browser-cli-rs` repository owns native builds, macOS signing/notarization, checksums, and COS publication. This repository verifies those immutable inputs and publishes only the lightweight npm wrapper.
